[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Handling Data Skew and Spill in Apache Spark"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Data skew and memory spill are two of the most common performance bottlenecks in Apache Spark. Data skew occurs when records are distributed unevenly across partitions, leading to a few overloaded tasks while the rest sit idle. Memory spill happens when a task runs out of allocated memory and spills intermediate data to disk, severely degrading execution speed."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Identifying Data Skew"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can identify data skew by inspecting the Spark UI during a shuffle operation, such as a join or groupBy. Look at the task metrics for the stage. If the 75th percentile duration is a few seconds, but the max duration is several minutes, you are dealing with data skew."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"Technique 1: Salting for Skewed Joins"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"Salting is a technique where you add a random prefix or suffix (a salt) to the skewed keys. This breaks up the heavy keys and distributes them across multiple partitions during the shuffle."},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"import org.apache.spark.sql.functions._

// Add a salt to the skewed DataFrame
val saltFactor = 10
val saltedDF = skewedDF.withColumn("salt", lit((Math.random() * saltFactor).toInt))
val saltedKeyDF = saltedDF.withColumn("salted_key", concat(col("skewed_key"), lit("_"), col("salt")))

// Broadcast or expand the other DataFrame to match the salt
val broadcastDF = referenceDF.crossJoin(spark.range(saltFactor).toDF("salt"))
val expandedKeyDF = broadcastDF.withColumn("salted_key", concat(col("ref_key"), lit("_"), col("salt")))

// Perform the join
val joinedDF = saltedKeyDF.join(expandedKeyDF, "salted_key")"},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Technique 2: Broadcast Hash Joins"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"If one of the datasets is small enough to fit into memory, you can avoid the shuffle phase entirely by using a broadcast join. This completely eliminates data skew caused by that join."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"import org.apache.spark.sql.functions.broadcast

val skewedJoinDF = largeDF.join(broadcast(smallDF), "id")"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding and Mitigating Memory Spill"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Memory spill occurs in operations like aggregations, joins, and sort operations when the working dataset exceeds the memory assigned to the task (Executor Memory * spark.memory.fraction * spark.memory.storageFraction). Look for Spill (memory) and Spill (disk) metrics in the Spark UI."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Increase partition count using spark.sql.shuffle.partitions to reduce the amount of data processed per task."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Increase executor memory or adjust spark.memory.fraction to give more headroom to execution memory."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Optimize complex objects and avoid unnecessary caching of large intermediate DataFrames that push execution memory out."}]
